data.definition: For this dossier, corporatism means structured state–group coordination or interest representation that privileges a limited set of organized bodies. It does not simply mean that corporations are large or politically influential.

data.analytical_boundary: Evidence of lobbying, advisory boards, or public–private contracts can support analysis of corporatist tendencies, elite coordination, or regulatory capture. It does not by itself establish a complete corporatist state.
failure_modes: Unequal access when well-resourced organizations receive privileged policymaking channels.
Opacity when bargaining moves from public institutions into private meetings, boards, or advisory forums.
Regulatory capture or agenda capture when regulated actors shape rules governing their own markets.
Weak accountability when public authority and private expertise become difficult to separate.
Exclusion of unorganized workers, consumers, small firms, dissidents, or communities without institutional representation.
Policy rigidity and cartelization when incumbent groups receive durable advantages over new entrants.
Conflict-of-interest risk when public mandates and private commercial opportunities overlap.

variants.description: Negotiated coordination among government, labor, business, and other organized groups under democratic institutions.
variants.name: societal or democratic corporatism

variants.description: The state licenses, structures, supervises, or constrains representative groups and may grant them monopolies over functional categories.
variants.name: state corporatism

variants.description: Sector-level coordination among government and selected organized interests without a fully corporatist national system.
variants.name: meso-corporatism

summary: Corporatism is a family of arrangements in which organized functional groups—such as business, labor, professional, religious, or civic bodies—receive structured access to representation or policymaking. It can exist in democratic, negotiated, sectoral, or authoritarian forms.
title: Corporatism — analytical definition and failure modes
